extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and principal investigators applying for NIH grants (R01/R21/K/K99/R03/R15 etc.) seeking practical advice about review, paylines, resubmissions, PO interactions, and award timing.
extracted.subtask_description: Practical Q&A guidance about NIH review outcomes, paylines, resubmission strategies, Program Officer interactions, timing (continuing resolutions/fiscal year), eligibility (ESI/continuous submission), JIT, and IC assignment for NIH grant applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative life of an application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can receive awards any time until they are administratively withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs rarely go back to fund an application from a prior FY, but it can happen if the IC wants to fund the science and prefers the A0 proposal over the A1 version. Discuss with your PO whether an older (still-active) A0 might be advocated for select pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission reviewer overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmitted applications (A1) may have at least one reviewer from the prior submission, but this is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether prior reviewers reappear depends on reviewer availability and whether they remain on the SRG; new reviewers can raise new concerns that change the panel outcome. Use the summary statement to understand whether reviewers flagged new issues or had concerns about changes you made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: When you receive the summary statement, use it to interpret reviewers' concerns and whether new issues were raised or prior weaknesses remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the summary statement with your PO to decide next steps (e.g., prepare a brief rebuttal for Program, submit a new A0 for insurance). The Summary of Discussion paragraph can reflect the panel's opinion and is useful to address in communications with PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer (PO) advocacy and select pay
rubrics_metrics.description: POs can help interpret summary statements and may advocate internally for select pay for meritorious applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your PO whether either application might be considered for select pay. POs may attend council meetings and can provide insight from discussions; they can request a brief written rebuttal from you to support advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline and percentile interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines (percentiles or impact score cutoffs) are IC-specific and determine which applications are likely to be funded; percentiles are often preferred over priority scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs estimate likely cutoffs based on prior years and application pools; payline changes are possible but usually small. When percentiles are available, ICs may use them over priority scores because percentiles reflect study section competitiveness across rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Announcement Set-Aside (PAS) funding behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: A PAS with an 'S' indicates set-aside money; PAS applications are typically judged against each other rather than the general payline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAS may state 'we intend to fund X meritorious applications' so R01 percentiles and paylines are less important — the program will prioritize highest-merit projects within the PAS pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and continuing resolution (CR) effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal budget delays (continuing resolutions) delay ICs receiving final appropriations and therefore delay funding decisions and issuance of NOAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs typically won’t know final appropriations until ~6–8 weeks after the federal budget is signed; some small/short-term awards may be made during CR, but most decisions and award processing are delayed until the appropriation is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility, resubmission rules, and new A0 vs A1
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit a new A0 in February and may apply more than twice if still eligible; a new A0 cannot reference prior applications (i.e., cannot be a resubmission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can't label a third submission as a 'resubmission' (A1) of the original; a new A0 must not mention prior applications. Check eligibility windows (e.g., ESI dates) and consider PO advice before deciding whether to resubmit or submit a new A0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-Stage Investigator (ESI) status & protection
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI status is determined by the Grants.gov successful submission timestamp; protecting that timestamp is critical to preserve ESI designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct Grants.gov time stamp by coordinating with your sponsored programs office and uploading/submitting with enough time to avoid errors that could change the timestamp. Ask about ESI extension policies if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission materials policy and timing for SRO
rubrics_metrics.description: Study section staff (SRO) typically will not send out updates submitted very close to the SRG meeting (e.g., within 30 days); inability to submit late updates does not change review status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs rarely distribute updates that arrive very close to meetings. If you submit post-review materials or publications after deadlines, your PO may be able to use them for select pay consideration, but they won’t retroactively change the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous (late) submission eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous (late) submission privileges are limited to currently appointed regular members of chartered NIH study sections and some other advisory bodies; temporary/ad hoc reviewers are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for continuous submission is indicated in your eRA Commons account. If you are a temporary or ad hoc reviewer, you cannot use continuous submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) and award processing
rubrics_metrics.description: JIT requests verify up-to-date information (IRB, Other Support, etc.) and trigger GMS/GMO award processing steps; award timing depends on IC processes and appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GMS/GMO handle award negotiation and will pay attention to details like overlapping support, budget reductions, and start dates. You may receive additional JIT requests when ICs are ready to process awards (often delayed by CR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary IC assignment and transfer likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary ICs almost never pick up applications; primary/secondary assignments and requests for transfer affect programmatic interest and funding likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application was routed to a different IC than you expected, contact POs at the relevant ICs to clarify interest and whether a transfer is possible. If the primary IC doesn't intend to fund, a transfer might be considered but is uncommon.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC funding decision factors beyond score
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs consider scientific merit, program priorities, portfolio balance, and availability of funds when making award decisions — not score alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even within similar percentiles, Program may prioritize projects that fit IC priorities or diversify portfolio balance. POs use these factors when advocating for or against funding specific applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred metric: percentiles vs impact scores
rubrics_metrics.description: When available, ICs often use percentiles over priority (impact) scores because percentiles reflect comparative competitiveness across review rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have both, emphasize percentile in PO discussions, but be ready to address concerns raised in the summary statement regardless of metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for contacting Program Officer (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact your PO for interpretation and next steps after you have the summary statement; POs may have limited insight before that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs can advise on whether to sit tight, prepare a brief rebuttal, request select pay consideration, or plan a resubmission. If scores or postings are delayed, contact SRO first about posting delays; PO won't have more info until summary statement or council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing overlapping support / multiple concurrent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs will check for scientific and budgetary overlap (Other Support) during JIT; overlapping aims/budgets must be resolved or one award will be reduced/eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to describe how you will eliminate overlap if both awards are funded; the IC that processes an award first typically funds full amount and the second award will be cut to remove overlap. Communicate proactively with both POs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism-specific timing & IC administrative practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Different ICs and mechanisms have different processing timelines and practices (e.g., NIAID may not issue K99 awards until July).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask the PO about typical award timing for your mechanism and IC. Some ICs defer decisions until specific windows or until they receive final appropriation information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expired FOAs and resubmission routing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PAR/RFA/FOA has expired, resubmitting to the parent or general FOA may change reviewer panels and assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your original FOA expired, you may have to submit to a parent FOA (A1 to parent), which could lead to different reviewers and different IC interest. Discuss FOA choice with your PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for insurance resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: When funding is uncertain (gray zone), POs commonly recommend preparing a resubmission for the next cycle as insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to address reviewer concerns in a resubmission and be mindful of eligibility windows (ESI, visa constraints). Preparing a new A0 can also be an insurance strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive payline changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IC raises its payline later in the fiscal year, the increase is typically applied retroactively to prior-reviewed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim paylines only cover awards made before final appropriation; final paylines set after appropriation may be applied to earlier-reviewed applications and affect funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: How ICs coordinate when multiple ICs have interest
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs and POs will communicate and try to coordinate funding decisions when multiple ICs have interest, but coordination is complex and timing-dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may ask the other IC to relinquish or take an application; if both ICs are interested, negotiations will address overlap and budget cuts. Be transparent with both POs so they can coordinate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous submission indicator location
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for continuous submission is indicated in your eRA Commons account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe you should have continuous-submission privileges (e.g., due to service), verify eRA Commons status and consult the continuous-submission policy page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-funded PI thresholds and Other Support scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs monitor 'well-funded PI' thresholds (institutional/IC caps) and will scrutinize Other Support during JIT and award processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit in JIT Other Support narratives about how you will handle partial overlaps or redistributed responsibilities if multiple awards are being considered. GMS/GMO will evaluate these details during negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical advice on communication tone and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect PO time, wait for summary statement to have a substantive discussion, and provide comprehensive but concise information when asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact POs with thoughtful, factual information (e.g., publication acceptance, eligibility constraints) and ask clear questions (e.g., whether to sit tight or resubmit). Over-sharing relevant details is usually helpful for PO advocacy.
